The Problem

You don't have a lead problem. You have a shared lead problem.

You've tried it: Angi, HomeAdvisor, Thumbtack. You pay for a "lead" that got sold to four competitors before your phone finished ringing. You race to call first, quote against three guys who'll go cheaper, and win maybe one in five — the price-shoppers.

Or you've run ads the old way: blasting a whole zip code and paying Google and Facebook to show your ad to renters, tire-kickers, and people who replaced their roof last year.

Here's the math nobody shows you: in a typical service market, fewer than 3 in 100 households are in-market for you this quarter. Old-way advertising pays to reach all 100. Shared-lead platforms make you fight over the three.

Both models are built so the platform wins whether you do or not.

The Solution

We stopped guessing who might buy. We find who's already deciding.

The EngageEngine™ — our buyer-identification system — reads the research trail homeowners leave before they ever pick up the phone: the searches, the review pages, the comparison visits. It resolves that activity to real, named people in your service area, and puts your ads in front of those people only — on Google, Facebook, YouTube, everywhere they go.

Why it works: an in-market homeowner behaves differently — they binge reviews, compare maps, check three websites in a week. That behavior is visible now in ways it wasn't three years ago. We simply refuse to spend a dollar of your money on anyone who isn't doing it.

And they're exclusively yours. One company per trade, per market. When you hold your territory, your competitor can't buy it. That's not a marketing tactic — that's the product.
